messages.subject: Difference between two spatial model specifications
parts:
Hi
I have seen these two types of spatial model specifications in this discussion group.
I would like to know the difference between them
1. y~alpha+f(id, model="bym")
2. y~alpha+f(id,w,model="bym")

where w is a weight vector. where each space index on id is associated to a each weight w. i.e id_i has weight w_i

Q1. how do I write the linear model?
Q2 how does it affect the CAR prior id?
Thanks. 
I look forward to hearing from you
Osafu

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Difference between two spatial model specifications
parts:
with this model

f(idx, )

then the contribution to the linear predictor is

x[idx]

where 'x' is the corresponding Gaussian component.

with

f(idx,weight, ...)

then the contribution to the linear predictor is

weight[idx] * x[idx]

by default, all weights are one.

H
